content_units: You have a strong base for a   junior data analyst   move without returning to school full-time. Your SaaS support background already maps well to analyst work in   customer insights, operations, product support analytics, and BI/reporting  .
- Current strengths: customer problem-solving, Excel, ticket/workflow knowledge, stakeholder communication
- Biggest gaps: Python, portfolio proof, analyst-focused resume/story
- Realistic target in 6 months:   entry-level/junior data analyst, support analyst, operations analyst, BI/reporting analyst
- Compensation target:   CAD 65,000–75,000   is realistic in Toronto/remote Canada for junior analyst roles, especially if you position into SaaS, operations, CX, or support analytics
With   8 hours/week for 6 months  , you have about   190–210 hours  . That is enough for a practical transition if you stay focused on job-relevant tools.

Month 1   Build analyst foundation   Refresh advanced Excel; solidify SQL basics; learn core metrics, joins, filters, aggregations; study business questions from support data   1-page skill tracker; SQL practice set completed
Month 2   Add visualization skills   Learn Tableau or Power BI; build 1 dashboard from CSV/Excel data; practice KPI storytelling   Dashboard project  1 published
Month 3   Start Python for analysis   Learn Python basics; pandas; CSV cleaning; simple charts; notebooks; reuse one prior dataset in Python   Small Python analysis notebook
Month 4   Create portfolio proof   Build 2 stronger projects tied to SaaS/support/customer data; write concise case studies; publish on GitHub/Notion   3 portfolio projects live
Month 5   Reposition for market   Rewrite resume; optimize LinkedIn; create target-company list; begin applications and networking   Analyst-ready resume + outreach tracker
Month 6   Execute job search   Apply consistently; tailor resume; practice SQL/Excel/case interviews; refine portfolio from feedback   40–80 targeted applications; interview readiness
Priority Skills for Junior Analyst Roles
Focus on skills in this order so your time compounds well.
Option 1:   SQL     Most important hiring filter for junior analyst roles   Key attribute: from basic to confident intermediate
Option 2:   Excel for analysis     Turn your existing strength into an obvious advantage   Key attribute: pivots, lookups, Power Query, charts
Option 3:   Power BI or Tableau     Needed to show reporting/dashboard ability   Key attribute: one tool is enough; Power BI may align better with many business teams
Option 4:   Python basics     Helpful but not required for many junior roles   Key attribute: enough for cleaning and simple analysis, not engineering
Option 5:   Business metrics thinking     Converts support experience into analyst credibility   Key attribute: churn, CSAT, resolution time, backlog, SLA, adoption
Option 6:   Data storytelling     Critical for interviews and dashboards   Key attribute: explain what changed, why it matters, what to do next
Best skill stack for your profile
-   Must-have:   SQL, Excel, one BI tool, portfolio, resume repositioning
-   Good-to-have:   Python basics, statistics basics, A/B test concepts
-   Skip for now:   machine learning, advanced engineering, deep math, full software-dev coursework
Portfolio Projects That Fit Your Background
Build projects that make your past experience an advantage rather than trying to look like a pure academic candidate.
Option 1:   Support Ticket Performance Dashboard     Analyze ticket volume, SLA, resolution time, reopen rate, and escalation trends   Key attribute: directly matches your SaaS support background
- Use sample help desk or customer support datasets
- Show KPIs by team, issue type, priority, and channel
- Include 3 recommendations such as staffing changes, macro usage, or process fixes
Option 2:   Customer Churn / Health Analysis for a SaaS Product     Segment accounts by usage/support patterns to identify churn risk   Key attribute: ties support work to revenue impact
- Analyze usage frequency, support contacts, response times, plan tier, and retention
- Build a dashboard plus short written insights
- Even if predictive modeling is basic, descriptive analysis is enough for junior roles
Option 3:   Knowledge Base Deflection and Self-Serve Insights     Measure whether help-center content reduces ticket volume   Key attribute: strong operations/CX analyst angle
- Compare article views vs ticket creation trends
- Identify high-volume issue categories that need better documentation
- Recommend which articles to improve to reduce support load
- GitHub repo plus a short portfolio write-up with screenshots
You are not “starting over.” You are a   data-minded SaaS support professional moving into analytics   with hands-on exposure to customer issues, operational workflows, and KPI improvement.

Data-oriented SaaS support professional with 3 years of experience analyzing customer issues, tracking service trends, and improving support workflows. Advanced Excel user with foundational SQL and growing experience in BI reporting and data analysis. Strong at translating operational data into clear insights for customer experience, process improvement, and business decisions. Seeking junior data analyst, support analyst, or operations analyst roles in Toronto or remote within Canada.
Convert task-heavy support bullets into metric/analysis bullets.
- Resolved customer support tickets and escalations
- Analyzed recurring ticket categories and resolution patterns to help identify process gaps and reduce repeated escalations
- Used Excel to track team performance
- Built Excel reports tracking ticket volume, SLA attainment, and resolution time trends to support weekly team performance reviews
- Synthesized customer issue data and product feedback to surface recurring friction points for internal support and product stakeholders
- Technical Skills: Excel, SQL, Power BI/Tableau, Python basics, GitHub
- Projects: 3 portfolio projects with tools and impact
- Core Competencies: reporting, KPI analysis, dashboarding, stakeholder communication, process improvement
Practical Job Search Strategy for Toronto and Remote Canada
Apply broadly across adjacent titles, not just “Junior Data Analyst.”
-   1.5 hours:   LinkedIn networking with Toronto/Canada analysts, ops managers, support leaders
Application strategy that works better than mass applying
- Prioritize roles requiring   SQL + Excel + dashboarding
- De-prioritize roles requiring heavy Python, R, ML, or 3+ years direct analyst experience unless the rest fits strongly
- Apply to   support-adjacent analyst roles first  , where your domain background is a differentiator
- Target companies where support data matters: customer success platforms, ticketing tools, SaaS operations teams
Message people with a narrow, credible story:
- moving into analytics through SQL/BI projects
- interested in support ops/CX/data analyst work
- asking for 15 minutes or advice, not a referral upfront
You do not need deep theory first. Prepare for:
- SQL joins, group by, where, case when
- Excel pivots, lookups, cleaning, summary charts
- KPI discussion: CSAT, SLA, AHT, FRT, backlog, churn indicators
- “Tell me about a project” using business problem → analysis → insight → recommendation
- Basic product/business sense: what metric would you track and why?
- you will choose   one BI tool   instead of both
- you are targeting   practical analyst roles  , not data science roles
- you will use your   support domain expertise as your wedge  , which is the fastest path to CAD 65,000–75,000 roles in Toronto/remote Canada
